study.title: Proverbs 22 - name, prudence, discipline and diligence
study.overview: Proverbs 22 gathers counsel that contrasts two ways: that of practical wisdom, which preserves life and produces favor, and that of folly, which brings ruin. The chapter values the good name above wealth, recalls that rich and poor belong to the same Creator, exalts the prudence that predicts evil, insists on the formation of children, calls to generosity with the needy, warns against bad companies and ends by stating that the skilled worker will be placed before authorities. Wisdom here is not only technical; it is moral and spiritual, for it leads to trust in the Lord.

outline.title: Good name, humility and fear of the Lord
outline.explanation: The first sayings compare reputation, wealth, social position and honor. The text teaches that a good name is worth more than material goods, that rich and poor depend on the same Lord and that humility accompanied by the fear of God brings lasting reward. The central idea is that human value is not measured by possession, but by the relationship with God and integrity.

outline.title: Dangerous Paths and Generous Life
outline.explanation: Here there are alerts about the perverse path, the need for instruction from an early age, the effects of oppression and the importance of a kind posture. The chapter shows that folly, violence, avarice and mockery disorganize the community, while generosity with the poor and the removal of the mockery promote peace and protection.

outline.title: Inner Purity, Discipline and Social Justice
outline.explanation: This part highlights the purity of heart, the graceful words, the care of God with the knowledge and uselessness of the lazy excuses. It also denounces the perverted woman and the oppression of the poor, including bribery. Biblical wisdom unites inner life, speaks right and just dealing with the vulnerable.

outline.title: Listen to the wise, flee from reckless debts and work with excellence
outline.explanation: The final section opens a collection of so-called sages and invites you to listen attentively to trust in the Lord and answer with truth. He then condemns the theft to the poor, the coexistence with iracundos, the reckless guarantees and the change of old landmarks. The closure culminates in the exaltation of the skilled man, who is placed before kings.

study.context: The chapter brings together short and practical proverbs attributed to the sapient environment of Israel. Tyndale's note notes that from 22:17 there is a section attributed to a group called "the wise" and that it opens with an appeal to hear, with the aim of producing trust in the Lord. It is also mentioned that there are thirty sayings, and that this collection can be compared to an ancient Egyptian composition in its organization, without this altering the biblical meaning of the text.
study.theology: Proverbs 22 presents a theological view in which God governs both personal life and social order. He is the Creator of rich and poor, the protector of knowledge, the defender of the afflicted and the judge of the oppressor. The fear of the LORD appears as a source of wealth, honor, and life, showing that biblical wisdom is not only human strategy, but a reverent response to God. The chapter also teaches that character is worth more than status, that discipline forms the heart and that excellence in work is a moral vocation before God. True wisdom yields confidence in the LORD and faithfulness in speech, in dealing with the weak and in daily conduct.

scholarViews.insight: Diligence and improvement of skills lead to better opportunities and placement in front of most prominent people.
The diligent and active man, even if he begins in a simple position, ends up being promoted and respected.
The industrious worker is favored and ends in a position of honor, even before kings.

questions: In which area of your life have you sought more resources than a good name and integrity before God and people?
What company habits, speaks and financial decisions need to be corrected so that you do not learn ways of anger, oppression or recklessness?
How can you demonstrate diligence and excellence in your work or study so that it serves God and bless others?
study.practice: Choose a concrete attitude for this week in each of these three areas: reputation, discipline and work. Preserve integrity in a difficult decision; practice a loving correction at home or with someone under your responsibility; and perform a task with whimsical and constancy, without laziness or improvisation. He also set a gesture of generosity for someone in need, remembering that the Lord defends the cause of the poor.
study.uncertainty: The exact historical context of the collection of 22:17 onwards is not clarified by the notes beyond the attribution to the "wise" and the possible structural similarity with an Egyptian composition mentioned by Tyndale. It is not possible to say more than that without extrapolating the sources provided. The interpretations of the commentators are presented as readings, not as definitive explanations of the text.
